faq.q: What is a team portrait template?
faq.a: A team portrait template is one portrait treatment for a whole staff page, plus a short intro if you want a voice. Every face starts from a photo that person approved. The sample is the teammate in the dark green shirt, set on a pale gray backdrop in a charcoal blazer.

faq.q: How does a team template become portraits and a video?
faq.a: Add each approved photo, set one backdrop, and save squares for the about page. A script can draft the intro, and an AI actor can speak it beside the row. The portraits stay photos of your teammates. A track can sit under that intro.

faq.q: Why use this instead of hiring a photographer or a creator?
faq.a: You skip the search for one date the whole staff can attend. A new hire can join the row when they send an approved photo. The same crop and light apply without a new booking.

faq.q: Who is a team template for?
faq.a: Small teams that should look like one staff on the site. A shop owner, a founder, and a hiring lead can all run the row from photos people already approved.

faq.q: Can a beginner make the set?
faq.a: Yes. The person who updates the about page can do this on a first try. They choose the treatment. Each approved photo supplies that face, and captions on the intro can be shortened in the editor.
A shop, a clinic front desk, and a software team all fit when the page should read as one staff. The treatment is the match. The trade they sell does not change the crop.

faq.q: Do I need permission to use a person's face in a team portrait?
faq.a: Yes. Each person agrees first. The result is not a passport or any other identity document. You may put the shop mark on the intro. Faces still come only from approved photos, and a clip filmed at work can sit under that intro.

faq.q: Which placements and sizes fit the intro?
faq.a: Square portraits stay on the site, and the intro can go to LinkedIn, a Story, YouTube, or an embed. LinkedIn is comfortable at 1:1, a Story wants 9:16, and an embed can be 16:9. Use 4:3 or 3:4 for a banner. Lengths are 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You can publish from a connected account.

faq.q: Do I need a paid plan to use a template?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A photo spends 24 credits. A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second clip spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. The total shows before the run, and a failed run returns the credits.

faq.q: Can I use the portraits and intro in ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes, if each person agreed to that use. The squares can go on the site and in a deck, and the intro can run as an ad for the shop. The download has no watermark. Another language can reuse the same portraits.

faq.q: Why start from a template instead of matching photos by hand?
faq.a: The treatment locks one backdrop and one crop, so a new hire can sit beside the owner without a layout you build by hand. Your own software can send approved photos through the API when the staff page needs that same crop. You can run every approved photo in one batch.

reviews.h2: How Small Teams Use Matching Headshots
reviews.lead: Example setups for a small team that wants one portrait style.

items.t: One framing on the About page
items.d: Example: the founders share one background, framing, and light. Each portrait still follows that person's own photo. Names sit in text beside the image.

items.t: A new hire joins the row
items.d: Example: a new teammate's approved photo uses the same background and framing. The rest of the team is not reshot.
Example: design and operations use the same portrait style, and each person keeps their own features.
Example: only a photo the teammate approved for business use is uploaded, and that person checks the result before it goes live.
Example: the same square portrait goes in a slide deck and a speaker bio. The job title stays as text, not lettering inside the image.
Example: the office uploads the approved photos together and gets one shared framing back for the team page.
Example: teammates in different cities upload their own approved photos and come back with one shared background.

items.t: A short intro beside the row
items.d: Example: the jobs page keeps the portraits, and a short clip with a voice and captions introduces the team.
Example: a press note uses the portrait and types the person's name and title underneath.

definition.title: What Is a Team Portrait Template?
paras: A team portrait template gives a whole staff page one backdrop, one crop, and one light, so everyone looks like they stood in the same room. Each portrait starts from a photo that person approved.
The portraits are ready for a site or a deck. Names stay in text beside the image, so a new job title does not force a new photo.

reasons.h2: Why Sellers Start From a Template
reasons.lead: A new hire can be on the about page before the next busy weekend, without a portrait day next month. One treatment is how a small shop does that.

items.d: The treatment runs on photos the team already approved, so the page does not wait on a studio hold.

items.t: Credits Instead of a Shoot Fee
items.d: Each portrait spends credits on whichever paid plan fits your team. Money you do not pay a portrait studio can stay on hiring and on ads.

items.t: More Than One Cut to Test
items.d: Render the row once, then a second intro line for a different audience. Keep the cut you want to publish.
Change a role in the text beside the photo, or rewrite the intro script and render again. A title change is not a new booking.

items.t: No Hold on a Creator Calendar
items.d: The treatment is ready when a new hire sends an approved photo. You are not waiting on a photographer's calendar.
The new hire inherits the same backdrop and crop, so you are not rebuilding a layout for one person. The spoken intro can say what they do.

more_sections.lead: The intro beside the portraits can carry a voice, captions, and music, while the portraits stay photos of your teammates.

items.d: A stock voice, or a clone from a short sample, can speak the short intro. The square portraits stay photos.
A name line or a one-sentence intro can sit on the clip, and you can move it in the editor. Job titles stay in text beside the portrait.

items.t: The Whole Team in One Pass
items.d: Every approved photo can run with the same background and crop, so the row matches in one pass.
Paste a public about-page link and the intro can start from the words already on that page.
The AI video agent can draft one spoken line about the team, and you can edit it.
A separate AI avatar can introduce the team while each portrait stays the person in the photo. Add B-roll of the shop or the product if the intro needs it.
A track from the music library can sit under the intro. The square portraits on the page stay stills.
You can set the crop, the light, and the background once, then reuse those choices for the next person.
The spoken intro and its captions can switch to another language while the portraits stay. Names on the page stay text you edit.
The intro can go to LinkedIn, YouTube, or to Facebook and Instagram, from the account you connect. The square portraits stay for the site and the deck.
Your own software can send photos through the API when a staff page needs the same crop.
